title: Federal government expands AI program with $500M boost
source_used: CTV News (article text in the page data); CBC News for the program name and total
key_facts: Canada's federal government says it is making an additional $500 million available over five years to help Canadian businesses adopt AI and bring Canadian-developed AI products to market (CTV News).

Support will focus mainly on sectors where Canada has expertise and growth potential: health and life sciences, energy and natural resources, transportation, agriculture, manufacturing and robotics; regional agencies can support other local priorities.

The expanded program will also help Canadian AI companies attract investment, secure customers and commercialize homegrown technologies, and funds organisations that give businesses specialised AI adoption expertise.
The government says the investment is meant to encourage broader AI adoption, help domestic AI firms grow while staying in Canada, and support growth and productivity.

CBC says the money is part of a $500 million pledge to expand the Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative to a total of $700 million, meant to help AI startups scale and tackle common adoption problems.
The announcement was made on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) at Deep Breathe, a London, Ontario, company, which receives about $1 million from FedDev Ontario for AI software that reads lung ultrasounds.
London MPs Arielle Kayabaga and Peter Fragiskatos spoke for Evan Solomon, Canada's minister of AI and digital innovation, who is also responsible for FedDev Ontario (CBC).
quote_evidence: The federal government says it is making an additional $500 million available over five years to help Canadian businesses adopt artificial intelligence technologies and bring Canadian-developed AI products to market.
The funding is part of a larger $500 million government pledge to expand the Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative to a total of $700 million.
why_it_matters_hint: Canada is adding $500 million over five years to help its businesses use AI and its AI firms grow at home.
